messages.subject: Probabilistic Reversal Learning Task - reward distribution of two stimuli
messages.subject_clean: Probabilistic Reversal Learning Task - reward distribution of two stimuli
messages.body_plain:
Dear Woo-Young,

I'm interested in using your hBayesDM package to model learning in my experiment. In my experiment we'd like to use probabilistic learning task, but I'm not sure about the reward distribution. In your article you say "In the probabilistic reversal learning task (PRL), there exists higher-order structure such that the reward distributions of two stimuli are anticorrelated (e.g. if one option has a reward rate of 80%, the other option has a reward rate of (100-80)%, which is 20%)." Specifically, I'd like to know if this anticorrelation of reward distribution of two stimuli should be perfect as in the above exaple.

In this paper for example http://science.sciencemag.org/content/304/5669/452.full, the authors used 2 stimuli, one of which was associated with a high (60%) probability of obtaining reward and the other one with or low (30%) probability of obtaining reward. These probabilities don't sum up to 100% as in your example and your definition of the PRL task.

What I would like to know is whether in such case, when the anticorrelation between reward distribution of two stimuli is not perfect, it is still fine to use the one of the models implemented in hBayesDM to model learning process?

Thank you for your help,
Emilia

messages.subject_clean: Probabilistic Reversal Learning Task - reward distribution of two stimuli
messages.body_plain:
Hi Emilia,

Glad to hear that you are interested in the package. If you are working on the learning task with two stimuli, try 'bandit2arm_delta' and also 'prl_*' models. True reward probabilities don't matter. O'Doherty et al (2004) Science paper used the temporal difference learning model. The model isn't included in the package but it should be very straightforward to implement the model.

Please try to follow an example as illustrated in this tutorial (http://rpubs.com/CCSL/hBayesDM) and let me know if you have any questions.

Best,
Young
